article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 65% Indica / 35% Sativa
Genetics: Super Lemon Haze × RS11
Breeder: Green House Seed Co.
THC Content: 28%
CBN Content: 0.20%
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Lemon Zest, Sour Citrus, Tropical Fruit
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 Weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: Early October
Indoor Yield: High
Outdoor Yield: Up to 1,700 g/Plant
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

The sharp fragrance of freshly squeezed lemons takes on an entirely different personality when surrounded by tropical candy sweetness and the unmistakable herbal character of classic Haze cannabis. Air Lemon brings these contrasting aromatic qualities together in a remarkably potent modern hybrid developed by Green House Seed Co. Created by crossing the legendary Super Lemon Haze with the highly regarded California cultivar RS11, the strain represents a meeting between two influential periods of marijuana breeding.

One parent contributed to the global popularity of citrus-dominant Haze genetics, while the other helped define the contemporary American market for exotic, fruit-forward cannabis. The resulting plant produces dense, colorful flowers with exceptional aromatic intensity and an unusually smooth, long-lasting psychoactive character. Despite containing predominantly indica genetics, its fragrance and genetic background retain much of the brightness associated with traditional sativa varieties. Vigorous branching, substantial production potential, and a comparatively short flowering period further distinguish this hybrid from many older Haze-influenced cultivars .
Genetics and Lineage

Air Lemon originates from a deliberate cross between Super Lemon Haze and RS11, also called Rainbow Sherbert #11. Green House Seed Co. selected these parents to combine the penetrating lemon fragrance and established performance of its award-winning Haze variety with the concentrated fruit sweetness of modern California cannabis genetics. Super Lemon Haze was originally developed from Lemon Skunk and Super Silver Haze , combining the citrus intensity of Skunk-related genetics with the vigorous growth and cerebral effects associated with traditional Haze breeding. Super Silver Haze itself carries Skunk , Northern Lights , and Haze ancestry, providing considerable genetic complexity. The resulting Super Lemon Haze became internationally recognized for its unmistakable citrus fragrance, powerful effects, and numerous cannabis competition victories, including High Times Cannabis Cup wins in 2008 and 2009 .

RS11 introduces a considerably newer genetic influence. Developed from the Rainbow Sherbert breeding work of Deo Farms, the celebrated #11 selection gained recognition through Wizard Trees and Doja Pak. Its ancestry is associated with Pink Guava and Sunset Sherbet , combining tropical fruit sweetness with creamy dessert characteristics and elements of the influential OZ Kush genetic family. Green House Seed Co. incorporated this highly regarded selection to strengthen the fruity, sweet-and-sour qualities of Super Lemon Haze while adding greater floral density. The finished hybrid is classified as approximately 65% indica and 35% sativa, demonstrating how crossing a strongly sativa-influenced classic with contemporary indica-leaning genetics can produce a plant that retains Haze characteristics without requiring the lengthy flowering cycle typical of older tropical varieties.
Effects and Experience

The psychoactive character of Air Lemon emphasizes a smooth, sustained experience rather than a brief burst of overwhelming stimulation. Its Super Lemon Haze ancestry introduces the potential for cerebral uplift, sensory engagement, and an increased appreciation for music or conversation, while RS11 contributes a more settled, physically comfortable dimension. The initial effects may involve an enjoyable change in mood accompanied by heightened awareness of familiar surroundings. Unlike some exceptionally stimulating Haze cultivars, the hybrid can feel more rounded, allowing mental activity and physical relaxation to develop together. Green House Seed Co. particularly emphasizes the long-lasting nature of the experience, with its persistent citrus and fruit flavors contributing to an impression of continued sensory intensity.

As the effects progress, a gradual sense of bodily ease may become more noticeable. Physical tension can feel less distracting, while the earlier mental stimulation may settle into a calmer, more reflective state. Experienced consumers may appreciate this combination during relaxed social gatherings, music listening, or unhurried recreational activities. Nevertheless, the breeder-reported THC concentration of approximately 28% places the cultivar among exceptionally potent marijuana varieties. Larger amounts can cause substantial intoxication, impaired coordination, reduced concentration, dizziness, or uncomfortable anxiety. Dry mouth, irritated eyes, and an increased heart rate are additional possible adverse effects. Its smooth reputation should not be interpreted as mild potency, and consumers with limited THC tolerance should approach the strain cautiously.
Medical Benefits

The combination of considerable THC potency and potentially relaxing physical effects may attract interest from medical marijuana consumers experiencing chronic discomfort or stress-related symptoms. Clinical research involving cannabis-based preparations has identified modest short-term benefits for some forms of chronic pain, particularly neuropathic pain. THC interacts with neurological pathways involved in pain perception, emotional processing, and sensory awareness, potentially altering how discomfort is experienced. However, these findings do not establish that every THC-rich cannabis flower will produce equivalent therapeutic outcomes. No controlled clinical trials have demonstrated that Air Lemon itself effectively treats pain or any other specific medical condition.

Its potentially uplifting mental character may also interest individuals seeking temporary mood improvement without the immediate heaviness associated with certain indica-dominant varieties. However, subjective euphoria should not be confused with an established treatment for depression, anxiety, or fatigue. High concentrations of THC can aggravate anxiety, trigger panic, and interfere with cognitive performance in susceptible individuals. The breeder reports approximately 0% CBD, meaning this cultivar should not be considered a balanced cannabinoid preparation. Frequent high-THC consumption may also contribute to tolerance, dependence, and changes in sleep quality. Medical consumers should discuss persistent symptoms, medication interactions, and potential risks with a qualified healthcare professional before relying on cannabis for symptom management.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Air Lemon’s fragrance is built around an unusually intense combination of sour citrus and concentrated tropical sweetness. Super Lemon Haze contributes the unmistakable sharpness of fresh lemon peel, accompanied by herbal Haze notes and a slightly resinous botanical background. RS11 introduces a softer, more elaborate fruit character resembling tropical candy, sweet citrus, and fruit sherbet. The combination creates an aromatic progression that begins with bright lemon acidity before developing into a sweeter, rounded fragrance. As the flowers approach maturity, the sour qualities become increasingly pronounced, producing a recognizable contrast between the two parental influences. Even light handling of mature buds can release a concentrated fruity aroma.

Although the cultivar’s aromatic characteristics are well documented by its breeder, a definitive ranking of its dominant individual terpenes has not been published. Limonene, terpinolene, beta-caryophyllene, and other compounds associated with citrus, herbal, and spicy cannabis aromas may contribute to its broader genetic background, but their actual concentrations require strain-specific laboratory testing. The recognizable fruit fragrance also depends on additional volatile compounds beyond the major terpenes commonly listed in cannabis testing results. During consumption, sharp lemon and Haze may dominate the initial flavor before transitioning into sweeter tropical fruit and a lingering sour-candy finish. Green House Seed Co. describes an unusually persistent taste that remains noticeable after inhalation and exhalation. Careful curing and airtight storage help protect the delicate aromatic compounds responsible for this distinctive sensory complexity.
Growing Information

Air Lemon develops a recognizable Christmas-tree structure, with a strong central stem surrounded by numerous productive lateral branches. The plant displays medium internodal spacing, creating enough separation between flowering sites to support light penetration while maintaining a substantial floral canopy. Its architecture combines the vigorous branching associated with Super Lemon Haze and the denser floral characteristics of RS11. Although the hybrid contains predominantly indica genetics, its growth can become relatively tall, particularly when plants receive an extended vegetative period. Indoor growers should therefore consider available vertical clearance and canopy management before flowering begins. Low-stress training may help distribute developing branches more evenly, while a Screen of Green arrangement can encourage consistent light exposure across the canopy.

Indoor flowering generally requires eight to nine weeks, considerably shorter than the maturation period associated with some traditional Haze varieties. The flowers develop a rounded appearance with slightly pointed upper sections, creating compact buds distinguished by relatively slender calyxes and pistils. Their dense structure contributes substantial visual appeal while keeping the leaf-to-flower ratio manageable. Green House Seed Co. notes that mature flowers are comparatively straightforward to trim, an advantage for growers handling larger harvests. Some phenotypes may develop attractive red and blue pigmentation during late flowering, creating additional contrast against the green foliage and resin-covered buds. These colors depend on genetic expression and environmental conditions rather than appearing uniformly in every plant.

The breeder classifies indoor yields as high without providing a standardized grams-per-square-meter figure. Outdoor plants can reach approximately 150–220 centimeters tall and potentially produce up to 1,700 grams of dried flower per plant under favorable conditions. Such figures represent exceptional production potential rather than guaranteed results. Harvest generally occurs at the beginning of October in the Northern Hemisphere. Strong lateral branches may require support as flowers gain weight, particularly on larger specimens. Adequate sunlight, balanced irrigation, reliable airflow, and appropriate humidity management are important as the compact buds mature. For cultivators seeking a productive citrus-dominant hybrid with contemporary fruit genetics, the strain offers a relatively manageable flowering period combined with considerable growth potential.
FAQ
Is Air Lemon an indica or sativa strain?

Air Lemon is an indica-dominant hybrid containing approximately 65% indica and 35% sativa genetics. Despite this classification, its Super Lemon Haze ancestry contributes distinctive citrus aromas and a potentially uplifting cerebral component, while RS11 introduces sweeter fruit characteristics and a more relaxing physical influence.
How strong is Air Lemon marijuana?

Green House Seed Co. reports approximately 28% THC, 0% CBD, and 0.20% CBN. These breeder-reported concentrations indicate exceptionally high psychoactive potency, although actual laboratory results may vary between harvests and individual plants. Its long-lasting effects can be intense, especially for consumers unfamiliar with high-THC cannabis.
What does Air Lemon taste like?

The flavor combines sharp lemon zest, sour citrus, tropical fruit, sweet candy, and herbal Haze. Super Lemon Haze contributes penetrating lemon characteristics, while RS11 introduces concentrated fruit sweetness and a sherbet-like finish. The flavor can remain noticeable for an extended period after consumption.
Does Air Lemon make you sleepy?

The cultivar is described as producing smooth, long-lasting effects rather than immediate heavy sedation. Its Haze ancestry may contribute mental stimulation, while RS11 can introduce a calmer physical component. Larger amounts may produce greater bodily heaviness and drowsiness, but individual responses depend on dosage and tolerance.
How long does Air Lemon take to flower?

Indoor flowering generally requires eight to nine weeks. Outdoor plants typically reach harvest maturity in early October in Northern Hemisphere climates. Under favorable conditions, mature outdoor specimens may reach 150–220 centimeters tall and produce up to 1,700 grams of dried flower per plant.
Final Thoughts on Air Lemon

Air Lemon brings together two important generations of cannabis breeding through an unusually complementary genetic pairing. The penetrating lemon fragrance and established Haze characteristics of Super Lemon Haze combine with the concentrated tropical sweetness and dense flowers of RS11, producing an aromatic profile that balances sharp acidity with rich fruit flavors. Its reported 28% THC concentration delivers substantial potency, while the smooth, enduring character of its effects distinguishes it from more aggressively stimulating or heavily sedating marijuana varieties .

For cultivators, vigorous Christmas-tree growth, compact flowers, an eight-to-nine-week flowering period, and substantial outdoor yield potential provide meaningful advantages. Its colorful late-flowering expressions and relatively easy-to-trim buds add further appeal, although larger plants may require additional branch support. Combining legendary Dutch Haze genetics with influential California fruit breeding, Air Lemon represents a distinctive modern hybrid that preserves the citrus intensity of classic cannabis while introducing the sweeter complexity of contemporary American cultivars.
